newsitem.title: GERMANY: German railway firm, Spiegel launch newspaper.
newsitem.headline: German railway firm, Spiegel launch newspaper.

text.p: The weekly news magazine Der Spiegel and Deutsche Bahn railway company said on Monday they had started a daily newspaper for German rail travellers aimed at business readers on late-afternoon express trains.

The daily, which will land on trains on Tuesday, will begin with a weekly circulation of 30,000 and appear at 4 p.m. local time. The two companies said they planned to double the weekly circulation to 60,000 by October.
Der Spiegel editor Stefan Aust said "the fastest daily newspaper in the world" would be transmitted electronically to express trains and printed and distributed on board.
"This newspaper marks a further step for the Spiegel along the way from print publisher to multimedia company," Aust said.

He said potential advertisers had shown strong interest in the four-page newspaper, which will be called "ICE-press" after the German ICE (inter-city express) trains, and that ad space for the first issues were already sold-out.
The newspaper will appear daily except Saturday and it will intially be distributed free in first class.
